report.incident_summary: The user reported that EC2 CPU utilization is above 90% and requested an investigation into resource saturation. Metrics show that CPU utilization was 88% to 97% with a mean of 93.75% over a 6-minute window, with 3 out of 4 samples above the 90% threshold. Memory utilization was between 54% and 56% with a mean of 55%, and no samples were above the 90% threshold. The severity and impact on the service are currently unknown.

severity_rationale.statement: CPU utilization was above the 90% threshold for a significant portion of the observed window, indicating potential resource saturation.

potential_root_causes.statement: High CPU utilization may be due to increased workload or inefficient processes.

uncertainty: Service impact and SLOs are unknown.
No evidence of memory utilization above threshold.
No evidence to establish a root cause.
recommended_steps: Review recent changes to the application or system that could have increased the workload.
Investigate the application logs for any errors or unusual behavior.
Check the system configuration and resource limits to ensure they are appropriate for the current workload.

report.incident_summary: The user reported a deployment failure and requested an investigation into the release events and startup failure. The deployment tool evidence shows that version v1.9.0 failed at 2026-10-22T09:00:00+00:00, just before the incident onset at 2026-10-22T09:01:00+00:00. Version v1.8.0 was rolled back at 2026-10-22T09:03:00+00:00, shortly after the incident onset. The health check for version v1.9.0 failed during rollout.

severity_rationale.statement: The deployment failure and subsequent rollback indicate a significant issue that may have impacted service availability.

potential_root_causes.statement: The failure of version v1.9.0 may have caused the incident.
The rollback of version v1.8.0 shortly after the incident onset may be a response to the incident.

uncertainty: Temporal proximity of the deployment events to the incident onset does not establish causation.
The correlation window is a heuristic and not a definitive causal link.
Service impact and SLOs are unknown.
recommended_steps: Review the logs and metrics for version v1.9.0 to identify the cause of the health check failure.
Investigate the rollback process to ensure it was executed correctly and did not introduce additional issues.
Monitor the service for any signs of instability or performance degradation following the rollback.
additional_information_required: Logs and metrics for version v1.9.0.
Details on the rollback process and any issues encountered.
Service impact and SLOs for the affected service.
